findings.message: 'paper_to_cite' unknown — Look for a data-descriptor paper (Scientific Data, Medical Physics, challenge paper).
'ethics_approval' unknown — For human data the paper should state ethics approval / consent.
'de_identification' unknown — How were names, dates, faces (head CT/MR!) removed?
'acquisition' unknown — Scanner vendors, sites, years, protocol. One scanner = poor generalisation.
'population' unknown — Who is included? Bias in age/sex/disease affects what your model learns.
'raw_data_available' unknown — For reconstruction: are raw projections/sinograms given, or only images?
'official_split' unknown — An official split makes your results comparable with published work.
'known_issues' unknown — Search '<dataset name> issues / errata / github issues'.
Custom / restricted terms: read the agreement (sharing, publication, storage rules).
9997 files, 62.90 GB on disk.
No README/LICENSE in the download: get licence & description from the source website.
All 9997 image files readable.
9997 samples (images or volumes) = 5118464 2D slices in total.
All images have the same in-plane size (512, 3).
Smallest image side is 3 px (< 256). Fine details may be lost.
9997 of 9997 images are not square.
Volumes: 512–512 slices (median 512).
Pixel size in mm is unknown (PNG/JPG/NPY carry none). No physical scanner geometry, no mm-based metrics (e.g. HD95 in mm). Check the paper for it.
Checked 30 random samples. Stored data type(s): float64.
Consistent intensity scale: normalised (0–1) (range 0 … 1).
No patient ID found (no DICOM tag, no PATIENT_ID_REGEX). You cannot prove a patient-level split → leakage risk. Find the ID in file names or a table.
No train/val/test folders found: you'll make your own split (per patient, fixed seed).
9997 of 9997 samples have no label.
No labels found.
No acquisition/demographic metadata in the files (typical for PNG/NPY). Get scanner, site, sex, age distribution from the paper or a metadata table.
91 exact duplicate files (e.g. ['ID_00e2957ab.npy', 'ID_021b4a7ce.npy']).
No near-duplicates among 300 sampled images.
No DICOM headers to check. Still look at the images for burned-in text, and at head scans for recognisable faces.
Modality not stored in the files — confirm it is CT.
Intensities are normalised (0–1): find the conversion to HU/μ in the docs, otherwise simulated projections are only relative.
Pixel size unknown → geometry in pixel units only.

Only reconstructed images → you'll simulate sparse projections yourself (standard practice). Avoid the 'inverse crime': simulate on a finer grid / different projector than you reconstruct with, and add noise.
Labels: none needed — the full-view image is the target. Note that the 'ground truth' is itself a reconstruction (noise, kernel, artefacts).
